english: What wild animal, mother, swims in the lake? That is an otter, and it eats fish. And who is that one? Its tail is broad. That one, the beaver, cuts wood with its teeth. Are they afraid of us? They are afraid of us because they hear us; it dives under the water. Be quiet and you will see them.
uncertain: h₁ésyo h₁orséh₂ pl̥th₂enéh₂ read as 'its tail (backside) is broad'

english: Lady, men are still standing at the river. How many men are there? Seven men. They carry spears. Are they guests/strangers? I do not know them. I do not know their tongue. Do not cross it, and do not throw a spear. Call the old men to the meeting place.
uncertain: h₁íd mē térh₂s: 'do not cross it (the river)'

english: Brother, let us track the aurochs. The aurochs is bigger than a horse and its horns are sharp. Have you seen the aurochs? I saw two aurochs at the lake. Now hear me. An aurochs killed our father's brother. Now let us go together with ten men. With ten men and many horses, may the gods protect us.
uncertain: last sentence: instrumental 'with ten men and many horses' attached to 'may the gods protect us'

english: Wife, I have killed an elk, and I bring you its liver. Who killed it? My spear pierced it. Now you will have a hide. What meat shall we share? Give a share to the old man (two old men?) and let us give the heart to the gods. The gods give us good things. I will cook the meat on the fire.
uncertain: kʷís h₁íh₂m̥ h₁ést — h₁ést unclear (ate? is?)
ǵérh₂onth₁e looks like dual, not dative singular

english: Whose hide is this, father? This is a bear's hide; I killed the bear in my youth. Tell me. How did you kill it? The bear came out of its den in winter. It stood up, and I threw my spear into its heart. Were you not afraid? I was afraid, but my hand did not tremble.
uncertain: wéwke moy is a perfect 3sg ('he has said to me'), not an imperative 'tell me'

english: At night I heard something. Is it a wolf? It is a wild beast. I fear the bear. Bears sleep in winter, and now it is winter. Kindle the fire and sit. Shall I stay awake? I will stay awake, and I will guard you through the night. Now I rest; the stars watch over us.
